h: Where to point the bikes, boots and the rest of your day
p: Hamsterley covers a big chunk of the hills on the edge of the Durham Dales, with Bedburn Beck running through the valley and the trees climbing up on either side. It is a forest that suits a lazy picnic by the water as much as a full-on day in the saddle.

Mountain bikers will find a range of graded trails, from gentle family-friendly routes on wide forest tracks to tougher, more technical runs for experienced riders, plus a skills area to warm up on. If you are new to it, start with an easier loop and work up. Walkers can choose from short waymarked routes around the visitor area or longer hikes up to quieter corners of the forest where you can go a good while without seeing another soul.

Allow at least half a day. With the play area, a picnic and a walk, families can easily fill a whole day without even thinking about the car. Pack plenty of layers, as the hills can feel chilly even when Bishop Auckland is bathed in sunshine.

On the way back, Bishop Auckland is well worth a stop. Auckland Castle, the historic home of the Prince Bishops of Durham, has been restored and opened to visitors, and the town also has the Mining Art Gallery and the Spanish Gallery around the Market Place. In summer, the open-air Kynren show tells the story of England on a huge outdoor stage. Head further up into Teesdale and you will reach the thundering waterfall at High Force, or go north to Durham to see the cathedral and castle on their wooded peninsula.
